schema_audit.grouping_justification: Columns melt_pool_width and melt_pool_depth are not separate columns in the published baseline parquet/csv splits (which contain 'id', 'label', and 'text'). Therefore, base measurement groups are identified by parsing the four fixed process parameters (material, power, velocity, beam_diameter) from the [SEP]-delimited 'text' column. During the paper's Lack-of-Fusion augmentation, these four parameters are held constant for each base melt pool while hatch_spacing and layer_height are swept. As a result, all rows sharing (material, power, velocity, beam_diameter) represent augmented siblings derived from that base melt pool.

methodological_implications:
DATA LEAKAGE CONFIRMED: 99.87% of validation samples share identical material, power, velocity, and beam diameter with samples in the training set.
Because the Lack-of-Fusion augmentation procedure created hundreds of sibling rows per base experimental measurement and subsequently applied a random split (75% / 15% / 10%) on the augmented dataframe rather than splitting base measurements prior to augmentation, virtually all validation cases represent near-exact duplicates of training points with identical Keyhole and Balling labels.
Consequently, high reported validation accuracy (e.g., 93.68% for Llama-Baseline) reflects interpolative memorization of augmented siblings rather than inductive generalization to unseen manufacturing regimes.
conclusion: CRITICAL_DATA_LEAKAGE: Near-complete cross-split contamination due to post-augmentation random splitting.
